summary.text: Tom Suozzi is the incumbent Democratic U.S. Representative for New York's 3rd Congressional District. An accountant and attorney by training, he was Mayor of Glen Cove and Nassau County Executive before first winning the House seat in 2016. He left Congress in 2023 to run for governor, then returned by winning a February 2024 special election. His campaign describes him as a co-chair of the bipartisan Problem Solvers Caucus and a member of the Ways and Means Committee.

paragraphs.text: Born August 31, 1962, in Glen Cove, New York, the youngest of five siblings; he graduated from Chaminade High School in 1980.
Earned a B.S. in accounting from Boston College in 1984 and a J.D. from Fordham University School of Law in 1989.

Worked as an auditor at Arthur Andersen and a certified public accountant, then as a federal court law clerk and a commercial litigator at Shearman & Sterling until 1993, according to his campaign website and Wikipedia.
Served as Mayor of Glen Cove from 1994 to 2001.
Served as Nassau County Executive from 2002 to 2009; he lost the 2009 county executive election to Ed Mangano and a 2013 rematch.

Ran unsuccessfully for the 2006 Democratic nomination for governor against Eliot Spitzer, and in 2007 was appointed by the governor to lead a state commission that proposed a property tax cap, according to his campaign website. He worked in the private sector, including at Harris Beach and Lazard, until 2016.
Elected to the U.S. House in 2016 and re-elected in 2018 and 2020; he did not seek re-election in 2022, running instead for the Democratic nomination for governor, which Kathy Hochul won.
Returned to the House by winning the February 13, 2024 special election to fill the seat vacated by George Santos, then won the November 2024 general election over LiPetri.

Serves on the House Ways and Means Committee (Oversight and Tax subcommittees); his campaign website says he was appointed to the House Select Committee on China and is Democratic co-chair of the Problem Solvers Caucus.
According to his campaign website, he lives in Glen Cove with his wife, Helene, and they have three children.
